reason: 'fruit binary or solitary', 'leaves solitary or binary' mean borne in pairs, as 'binate' was mapped on 2026-11-14; 'inflorescence sometimes binary' reads the same way.

label: catkin-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's architecture resembling a catkin, a dense, often pendulous spike of small, reduced, usually unisexual flowers. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991142 spike-like; the inflorescence itself is PO:0030119 catkin inflorescence.
reason: The same class the second-model review proposed on 2026-11-14 ('catkin-like'), which is not yet in flopo_flora_value_terms.tsv; this spelling should become its synonym, not a second class. FLOPO:0991232 julaceous is for leafy moss shoots, not inflorescences.
Bearing corky lenticels: lenticel present, as the rule for 'lenticellate'; 'corky' (FLOPO:0991126) is a quality of the lenticels and can be added as a second statement on the lenticel.

Surfaces covered with minute scales are scaly; 'covered' alone was rejected because the covering is the quality, and here the covering is named. The scale shapes in the truncated examples stay in the record.

target: new: conjunction of two qualities (dentated PATO_0001205 + ciliated PATO_0001408)
reason: A margin that is both minutely toothed and fringed with fine hairs: two qualities at once, not a continuum and not a single term (as 'obliquely rounded').
Deplanate (Latin deplanatus) means flattened or levelled; it applies to the pappus bristles and to the capsule apex.
The texture of a dried specimen: coriaceous with the specimen condition 'dry' and the degree word 'thinly' kept in the record.

It means 'callus absent' on the orchid lip, but there is no usable callus class (PO_0005052 is culture callus and FLOPO_0986120 is the grass floret callus), so 'ecallose' was rejected on 2026-11-14; same decision here.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: free part of gynostemium FLOPO_0986015 + length PATO_0000122)
reason: Not a quality word but a parser label: the statements give the length of the free part of the column, a region of the gynostemium, so it is a measurement on a region and needs no term.

label: heteropolar
definition: An asymmetrical quality inhering in a pollen grain or spore by virtue of its proximal and distal faces differing in shape, ornamentation or apertures, so that it is not symmetric about its equatorial plane. NOTE: Palynological; opposite of isopolar (proposed 2026-11-14). PATO polarity terms concern cell polarity, not this symmetry.
reason: A standard palynological polarity term with no PATO or FLOPO equivalent; it pairs with the isopolar class proposed in the previous second-model review.

target: docs/odp/18-position-of-the-bearer.md (lobe with position lateral FLOPO:0991380 + width PATO_0000921)
reason: A width measured on the lateral lobes of the leaf blade or lip: a positioned part with a measurement, not a quality. The example 'lip: ca. 3 mm wide' is the width of the whole lip.

target: docs/odp/13-indefinite-count.md (several flowers) + arrangement of member parts (flower PO_0009046 + loose PATO_0001802)
reason: Combines the indefinite count 'several-flowered' (pattern 13, 2026-11-14) with 'laxly flowered', which the same review sent to the member-arrangement pattern.
Bark splitting lengthwise is bark marked by cracks; FLOPO fissured (synonym cracked) covers bark and axes. The direction can stay as a cue in the record.
A middle value of thickness with no stated scale or reference (Carex culms 'medium thick'); PATO normal thickness means compared with wild type and does not fit.

target: new: two values of one bearer (spherical PATO_0001499 + asymmetrical PATO_0000616)
reason: As 'obliquely ovate' and 'obliquely obovate' on 2026-11-14: the body is globose and unequal-sided, so both qualities hold and no new term is needed.

target: new: conjunction of two qualities (obtuse PATO_0001935 + apiculate, grounded to PATO_0000944)
reason: An obtuse apex ending in a short abrupt point: two qualities of one apex together, not a continuum between them.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: ovate FLOPO:0991024 – rhomboid PATO_0001938, with 'sub' from docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md)
reason: A compound of two shape values, as 'ovate-rhombic' and 'subrhombic' were handled on 2026-11-14.

target: new: division of the parts of the bearer (leaf pinnate PATO_0000410 + pinna FLOPO_0985027 pinnatisect FLOPO:0991155)
reason: A frond that is pinnate with pinnatisect pinnae: two statements on the leaf and on its pinnae, as with the region and part-of-the-bearer patterns; the prefixed numbers ('3-pinnate-') are the degree of division.
Poculiform means goblet- or cup-shaped, as 'cupuliform' was mapped on 2026-11-13.
An inflorescence type, a panicle whose branches are racemes: it names a part, not a quality. The racemose branching can be added with FLOPO:0991197 raceme-like on the branches if needed.

target: new: arrangement of member parts (flower PO_0009046 part of the inflorescence + distant FLOPO:0991189)
reason: Flowers spaced far apart along the axis: the member-arrangement pattern used for 'laxly flowered', with FLOPO distant as the value; counts like '5-12-flowered' go to pattern 03.
Foveolate is minutely pitted, i.e. foveate (rule C179 for 'pitted'); 'reticulately' describes the ridges between the pits and could be added as FLOPO:0991100 reticulate.
Saffron is a deep orange-yellow colour of flowers and filaments.
Half-pendent is an approximate degree of pendent, like the 'sub-' words, not a separate orientation term.

target: new: conjunction of two qualities (serrulate FLOPO:0991081 + scabrous FLOPO:0991058)
reason: Margins rough with minute forward-pointing teeth (sedge leaves and bracts): both qualities hold of the margin, so two statements rather than a term.
Leaves inserted singly along a spiral are exactly FLOPO spirally arranged; 'alternate' adds nothing to it.

target: new: conjunction of two qualities (lanate PATO_0104357 on the part + hair star shaped PATO_0002065)
reason: A woolly indumentum of stellate hairs: the pilosity of the part and the shape of its hairs, which is how 'stellate' was treated (a quality of hairs) on 2026-11-14.
Arising almost from the base: 'radical' is a synonym of FLOPO basal, and 'sub-' is the approximate-value qualifier.

label: tendrillate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being modified wholly or in part into a slender, coiling tendril. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991247 flagelliform and FLOPO:0991230 spine-like; used for inflorescences (Adenia, Vitaceae) whose axis ends in or becomes a tendril.
reason: The PO tendril classes are leaf, leaflet, branch and stem-apex tendrils and none is an inflorescence tendril, while 'tendril' alone was rejected as generic. A quality of the inflorescence therefore states it without a doubtful part.
A compound of two shape values, handled by the continuum relation as 'obovate-triangular' was on 2026-11-14.
